solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dope confused by rhythm heard in walker's recorder

indicators.note: confused means the letters of the word dope are jumbled into a new order
heard signals that a word for rhythm is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: metre is the rhythm of verse

explanation.surface: Some drug addled by a beat ends up in a hiker's gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: PEDO is the anagram of DOPE ('confused'); METRE is said aloud ('heard') and written the American way, METER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedometer is a device that counts the steps taken by someone on foot.

clue.text: Got expert back to health

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
someone cured has been restored to health

explanation.surface: A specialist nursed someone back to health.
explanation.definitionFit: To procure is to obtain, a synonym of get in the past tense.

clue.text: One may cross and another may make one cross

definitions.text: One may cross and another may make one cross

parts.words: One may cross and another may make one cross
parts.note: a slanting line runs across a square from corner to corner, and a second such line drawn the other way forms an X shape

explanation.surface: A riddle about crossing and annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' is first a verb (to go across) and then the noun shape X; the surface hints at the adjective meaning angry.
explanation.definitionFit: A slanting line joining opposite corners crosses a shape, and two of them form an X.

clue.text: Medal I damaged is put in the post

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of medal and I are knocked into another order

explanation.surface: A medal I broke gets sent off by mail.
explanation.definitionFit: To mail something is to send it through the postal system.

clue.text: Mosquito's keeling over, lady heartlessly snarled

indicators.note: keeling over, in a down clue, turns the insect word upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: a mosquito is a kind of gnat

indicators.note: heartlessly removes the central letters of the word lady

explanation.surface: A mosquito tips over while a woman snaps cruelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeling over' reverses GNAT to TANG; 'heartlessly' takes AD from LADY, leaving LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Snarled hair or string is knotted and matted, which is the adjective tangly.

clue.text: Examination to go through again?

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to search is to go through something looking

explanation.surface: Is a study just going over the same ground a second time?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split RE-SEARCH, searching once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Research is careful study or investigation of a subject.

clue.text: Frenchman in RADA performing this?

indicators.note: in places the French title inside the other letters
performing means the letters of the acting school's name are put through their paces in a new order

parts.note: M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A Frenchman training at London's acting school would do this.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is London's Royal Academy of Dramatic Art; 'performing' rearranges it to DRAA, and M goes 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plays and theatre are what students at an acting academy perform.

clue.text: Singing as couple expected, couple of times in middle of night

parts.note: something due is expected
T is short for time, so two of them give TT

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letter of the word night

explanation.surface: A pair crooning on schedule, twice, at midnight.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing a duet means two people singing together.

clue.text: Beaming as a good meal's dished up

indicators.note: dished up means the letters of meal are served in a different arrangement

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A diner smiles when a tasty dinner is served.
explanation.definitionFit: Agleam means shining or glowing, as a beaming face does.

clue.text: Strange island where some volcano lava's turned up

indicators.note: turned up, in a down clue, reads the letters from bottom to top, so backwards
some says only part of the words volcano lava's is used

explanation.surface: An eerie isle where lava from a volcano has erupted.
explanation.walkthrough: NOLAVA sits across 'volcano lava's', and 'turned up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Avalon is the mythical isle of Arthurian legend, a fittingly strange place.

clue.text: Applause for speech when ranting initially gives way to verse

indicators.note: gives way to means one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word ranting

explanation.surface: A speaker is cheered once the tirade gives way to poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: In ORATION the R (first of 'ranting') is replaced by V.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovation is a burst of clapping from an audience.

clue.text: Very much a bargain?

definitions.meaning: a lot, as in 'it matters a lot'
read whimsically as an excellent deal

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a lot, and read literally it describes a superb transaction.

clue.text: Opening 24 hours when payment's due

parts.note: a rent is a tear or opening
a day lasts twenty-four hours

explanation.surface: A shop's first day of trade coincides with the bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like a launch; it is a noun meaning a split or gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The day the tenant hands over money to the landlord is the day this phrase names.

clue.text: Train worker for bar staff

parts.note: a rail is a bar
to man is to staff

explanation.surface: Someone on the trains swaps to working behind a pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar staff' reads as one phrase meaning pub workers; here the words part company, a rod and a verb meaning to crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A railman is someone employed on the railways.

clue.text: Trucker may do this drive — told he goes wrong

indicators.note: goes wrong signals that the letters of drive, told, he and goes are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lorry driver is warned his route has gone astray.
explanation.definitionFit: A haulier's job is to bring cargo to its destination, and the idiom also means succeed as promised.

clue.text: Strong port, ours had been stirred!

parts.note: Vigo is a port in northwest Spain

indicators.note: had been stirred means the letters of ours are mixed up

explanation.surface: A fortified wine of ours has been mixed!
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink; it is the Spanish harbour. 'had been stirred' gives ROUS from OURS.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigorous means robust, full of strength and energy.

clue.text: Reasonable allowance has a learner's support

indicators.note: has signals that the allowance word takes on the pieces that follow
support, in a down clue, places these letters underneath, holding up the first part

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A fair amount of pocket money comes with a learner's backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Rational means sensible and based on reason.

clue.text: Dismissed one side entirely

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
right is one side, the other being left

explanation.surface: A batsman is sent off, the whole team on one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means completely or wholly.

clue.text: Tender visitor at Christmas

definitions.meaning: one who tends, here of flocks
in the Nativity story, herdsmen came to see the baby Jesus

explanation.definitionFit: A sheep minder looks after animals, and such men visited the manger at the first Christmas.

clue.text: Stout German's good results in big corporation

parts.note: stout is a dark beer
gut is the German word for good

explanation.surface: A hearty German enjoys success at a large firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is an old humorous word for a large belly. 'Stout' looks like an adjective; it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is a jocular old term for a paunch, and a beer belly is a large one.

clue.text: Happened to be going over hill

indicators.note: going over, in a down clue, puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: the infinitive to be is shortened to its verb, be
a fell is a hill in northern England

explanation.surface: Something occurred on the way across a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: FELL is a word for a hill used in England's Lake District and the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Befell is the past tense of befall, meaning happened or occurred.

clue.text: Recruit for combat?

definitions.meaning: to take on or hire someone

explanation.definitionFit: To engage staff is to hire them, and to engage the enemy is to fight.

clue.text: Dance arranged in silence

indicators.note: in places the arranged word inside the silence word

parts.note: to mute is to silence
set means arranged

explanation.surface: A routine performed in quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A musette is a pastoral dance, named after a small bagpipe.

clue.text: The compiler's illusion, falling short of the European system

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

indicators.note: falling short drops the final letter of the illusion word

parts.note: a trick can be an illusion

explanation.surface: The setter's sleight of hand fails to match the Continent's way of doing things.
explanation.definitionFit: The metric measurement system is the standard used across Europe.

clue.text: Plan sure to capture very loud bear

indicators.note: to capture puts the loudness letters inside the rearranged ones
plan, as a verb, means the letters of sure are set out in a new design

parts.note: FF is fortissimo, very loud in music

explanation.surface: A scheme certain to trap a noisy bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plan' is an unusual anagram signal: to plan is to lay letters out afresh, giving SUER, which 'to capture' wraps around FF.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to endure or put up with it.

clue.text: Understand number's wrong

parts.note: a figure is a number
out can mean mistaken, as in your sums are out

explanation.surface: Realise that a figure is incorrect.
explanation.definitionFit: To work out or comprehend something is a common idiom for grasp.

clue.text: Whistle-blower with no right to encourage Eastern asylum seeker

parts.note: a referee blows the whistle

indicators.note: with no removes the letter for right from the encouragement word

parts.note: to urge is to encourage

explanation.surface: An informer without rights encourages an Eastern migrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistle-blower' suggests an informer; it is a referee. 'with no' takes R from URGE, giving UGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A refugee is a person fleeing their country and seeking sanctuary.

clue.text: City grounds holding 500

indicators.note: holding means the dregs word wraps around the numeral

parts.note: lees are dregs or grounds
D is 500 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A city's stadiums can hold five hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grounds' suggests football grounds; it is coffee grounds, sediment.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in Yorkshire in northern England.

clue.text: Torn material gets valued

parts.note: lace is a delicate material
rated means valued

explanation.surface: Ripped fabric is still appraised.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerated means cut or torn, especially of flesh.
